articles.title: PSX Closes at Record 175,380 as KSE-100 Gains 3,366 Points for a Second Day
articles.description: The KSE-100 surged 3,366.38 points, or 1.96%, to close at a record 175,379.86 on Thursday, its second straight session of gains of more than 3,300 points, as easing geopolitical fears and falling oil prices kept buyers in control.
articles.sources: Business Recorder, UrduPoint, ARY News, The Express Tribune, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange continued its strong positive trend on Thursday, gaining 3,366.38 points, a positive change of 1.96 percent, to close at 175,379.86 points against 172,013.48 points recorded in the previous trading session, Business Recorder, UrduPoint and ARY News reported on November 5.

A record close after a volatile session

The market opened on a positive note, with the index initially surging to an intraday high of 176,604.51. Profit-taking then emerged, triggering a sharp correction that pushed the index towards its intraday low of 174,291.25, before buyers returned and the benchmark settled at its record close. Trading volume on the all-share index increased to 999.81 million shares from 841.61 million in the previous session, and total market capitalisation rose to Rs19.113 trillion from Rs18.777 trillion. The local unit closed the day at 276.67 against the US dollar, a gain of Re0.03. According to market data, 362 shares rose, 124 fell and 34 did not move during the session.

Two days, more than 7,300 points

Thursday's gain followed Wednesday's surge of 3,994.62 points, or 2.38 percent, to 172,013.48 — one of the market's strongest single-session gains — meaning the benchmark has added more than 7,300 points in two sessions. Reports attributed the rally to institutional buying and improving sentiment over geopolitical developments following the US midterm election results, alongside easing international crude oil prices. Business Recorder reported that buying continued amid expectations that losses suffered by US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in this week's Congressional elections may reduce the risk of further escalation of the US-Israeli war on Iran, while Brent crude had fallen to about $101.85 a barrel during Wednesday's session.

What traders watch next

Whether the momentum holds will depend on those geopolitical threads and on Friday's US jobs report, which global markets are watching, as noted in Wednesday's coverage. Two sessions do not make a trend, and the sharp midday correction on Thursday showed that profit-taking is never far away at these levels. For now, though, the market has crossed the 175,000 milestone for the first time, and the breadth of Thursday's advance — hundreds of shares higher on nearly a billion shares traded — suggests participation has broadened beyond a handful of heavyweights.

articles.title: ABHI Microfinance Bank IPO Book-Building Opens Today, Bidding Runs November 5-6
articles.description: Book-building for ABHI Microfinance Bank's IPO of 132 million shares opens on November 5, with institutional investors bidding between Rs15 and Rs22.50 a share ahead of public subscription on November 12 and 13.
articles.sources: Profit by Pakistan Today, The News, ProPakistani, October 30 - November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Book-building for the initial public offering of ABHI Microfinance Bank begins on Thursday, November 5, with institutional and high-net-worth investors able to bid for 99 million shares over two days, according to details disclosed to the Pakistan Stock Exchange and reported by Profit by Pakistan Today, The News and ProPakistani.

How the offer is structured

The bank plans to raise between Rs2 billion and Rs3 billion through an IPO of 132 million ordinary shares. The book-building portion comprises 99 million shares, or 75 percent of the total issue, at a floor price of Rs15 per share, including a premium of Rs5 over the Rs10 par value. The price band allows bids to rise up to 50 percent above the floor, to a maximum of Rs22.50 per share. At the floor price the offering would raise about Rs1.98 billion, and at the ceiling about Rs2.97 billion. The remaining 33 million shares are reserved for the general public, with retail subscription scheduled for November 12 and 13. The public portion is fully underwritten by Arif Habib Limited, Topline Securities Limited, Growth Securities (Private) Limited and Dawood Equities Limited, with the first three also acting as joint lead managers.

Dates investors need to know

The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan has approved the prospectus, and the PSX has approved the schedule for publication of the prospectus, book-building and public subscription. Registration of eligible participants runs from November 2 to 6, closing at 3 pm on the final day, with expressions of interest to the National Clearing Company of Pakistan between November 2 and 6, and bidding from 9 am to 5 pm on November 5 and 6. Ownership disclosures show ABHI (Private) Limited holding a 73.73 percent stake and TPL Corp Limited the remaining 26.27 percent.

What the bank plans to do with the money

The bank said gross proceeds at the floor price would primarily be used to expand its loan portfolio and strengthen its capital base. Management estimates a profit of about Rs1.5 billion in the second half of 2026, taking the projected full-year profit to around Rs3 billion — a management forecast, not a reported result. The final IPO price will be set by institutional demand during book-building, not by the floor price alone, so the two days of bidding will decide how much the bank actually raises. Investors watching the issue will also note that the offering comes in what reports have called Pakistan's busiest-ever IPO year, with several listings competing for attention in the same weeks.

articles.title: PSX Surges 3,995 Points to Close Above 172,000 on Geopolitical Optimism
articles.description: The KSE-100 surged 3,994.62 points, or 2.38%, to close at 172,013.48 on Wednesday, one of its strongest single-session gains, as institutional buying followed the US midterm results and easing oil prices.
articles.sources: Business Recorder, UrduPoint, ARY News, Express Tribune, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange witnessed a strong bullish session on Wednesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index gaining 3,994.62 points, or 2.38 percent, to close at 172,013.48 points, Business Recorder, UrduPoint and ARY News reported on November 4.

The session

The index had closed at 168,018.87 points in the previous session, after Tuesday's 1,454.80-point gain, and traded between an intraday high of 172,287.00 and a low of 168,355.26 on Wednesday. Trading volume jumped to 841.6 million shares from Tuesday's 517.3 million, with the value of traded shares at Rs35.3 billion, and total market capitalisation rising to Rs18.777 trillion from Rs18.396 trillion. The market opened strongly, gaining 1,707.48 points to 169,726.34 by 10:04 a.m. and crossing 170,000 in the early minutes of trading.

What drove the rally

Reports attributed the rally to institutional buying and improving sentiment over geopolitical developments following the US midterm election results, alongside easing international crude oil prices — Brent crude fell to about $101.85 a barrel during the session. On Tuesday, easing oil prices and optimism over potential negotiations between the United States and Iran had already lifted sentiment. Whether the momentum holds will depend on those geopolitical threads and on Friday's US jobs report, which global markets are watching.

articles.title: Pakistan Ranks 106th on 2026 Global Hunger Index as Report Questions Budget Priorities
articles.description: Pakistan scored 25.5 on the 2026 Global Hunger Index, ranking 106th of 122 countries, according to a report cited by IANS on November 4, which contrasts rising defence spending with a health allocation of PKR 53.3 billion.
articles.sources: IANS via Ten News, European Times, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan scored 25.5 on the 2026 Global Hunger Index, placing it 106th among 122 countries and worse than every functioning state in South Asia, according to a report cited by IANS on November 4 — figures presented here as reported, not independently verified by this site.

The reported figures

According to the report, published in the European Times news portal and cited by IANS, undernourishment affects 16.1 percent of the population, child stunting among under-fives stands at 33.6 percent, child wasting at 9.8 percent and under-five mortality at 5.6 percent. The federal budget for 2026-27 allocated PKR 3 trillion to defence services, up 17.6 percent, with the physical assets line for weapons procurement rising 39.6 percent to PKR 925.8 billion, while health received PKR 53.3 billion in total, of which PKR 24.3 billion covered the health and nutrition development portfolio.

The wider context

The report notes that the government's own Economic Survey records public health expenditure at 0.8 percent of gross domestic product, and that military pensions, carried separately at PKR 822 billion, exceed the full health allocation more than 15 times over. It also notes that Pakistan abolished the wheat support price mechanism under reforms tied to its IMF programme, then presided over procurement that collapsed to roughly 480,000 tonnes in Punjab against a three million tonnes target. These are the report's claims as relayed by IANS; official responses to the report had not been published at the time of writing.

articles.title: PSX Gains 1,454 Points to Close at 168,018 on Renewed Buying in Heavyweights
articles.description: The KSE-100 gained 1,454.80 points, or 0.87%, to settle at 168,018.87 on Tuesday as bargain hunting in banks, fertilisers and cements lifted the market despite US-Iran tensions.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, Business Recorder, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange extended its recovery on Tuesday, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index gaining 1,454.80 points, or 0.87 percent, from the previous close of 166,564.07 to settle at 168,018.87, as investors returned to heavyweight stocks for bargain hunting, The Express Tribune and Business Recorder reported on November 3.

A broad-based session

The benchmark opened on a positive note and maintained its upward trajectory, touching an intraday high of 168,469.78 and a low of 167,308.66. Buying was broad-based, led by commercial banks, fertilisers, cements and investment banks, with Fauji Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, HBL, Pakistan Services, Meezan Bank and Engro Fertiliser among the major contributors. Trading volume rose to 517.3 million shares from Monday's 443.4 million, with the value of traded shares at Rs20.7 billion. Cnergyico PK was the volume leader with 114.9 million shares traded, closing down Rs0.54 at Rs11.74.

Geopolitics in the background

The positive momentum persisted despite mounting geopolitical uncertainty, as reports of a United States strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official's remarks that Tehran and Washington remained far from a deal kept investors cautious. Brent crude rose 1.3 percent to $106.13 a barrel by midday GMT. Sentiment also received support from President Trump's indication that the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, raising hopes of a potential diplomatic breakthrough, KASB KTrade noted.

articles.title: Pakistan's First SPAC Deal Brings Solar Firm Ningbo Green Light Energy to the PSX
articles.description: Ningbo Green Light Energy has joined the PSX Main Board, completing Pakistan's first-ever SPAC transaction, after LSE SPAC-I merged into the solar engineering company.
articles.sources: Nukta, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange has welcomed Ningbo Green Light Energy Limited (NGLEL) to its Main Board, marking the successful completion of Pakistan's first-ever Special Purpose Acquisition Company (SPAC) transaction, Nukta reported on November 3.

How the listing worked

NGLEL was originally identified as the target company of LSE SPAC-I Limited. It completed the business combination through a Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the Lahore High Court on September 30, 2026. The transaction, structured and facilitated by LSE Capital, resulted in the merger of LSE SPAC-I into NGLEL, paving the way for the solar energy company to become publicly listed.

What NGLEL does

NGLEL operates in the renewable energy sector, specialising in solar engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), system integration, and operations and maintenance services. Speaking at a gong ceremony hosted by the PSX to mark the listing, PSX Director Ahmed Chinoy said the transaction marked a landmark achievement for the country's capital market, demonstrating how the SPAC framework can offer businesses an alternative route to access public markets.

articles.title: PSX Recovers 155 Points to Close at 166,564 as Oil Prices Ease
articles.description: The KSE-100 climbed 154.81 points, or 0.09%, to settle at 166,564.07 on Monday after dipping to 165,776 intraday, as falling global oil prices and hopes of diplomatic progress in the Middle East offered relief.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, Business Recorder, Arif Habib Limited, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange staged a late recovery on Monday to close marginally higher, reversing an earlier decline as investors weighed hopes of diplomatic progress in the Middle East against persistent selling pressure, The Express Tribune reported on November 2.

A volatile session

The benchmark KSE-100 index climbed 154.81 points, or 0.09 percent, to settle at 166,564.07 points, after remaining under pressure for much of the session and falling to 165,776.85 at 12:29 p.m., down 632.40 points from the previous close of 166,409.25. Buying was led by Mari Energies (up 3.15 percent), Fauji Fertiliser (up 0.92 percent) and Engro Holdings (up 1.57 percent), while Attock Refinery (down 10 percent), Oil & Gas Development Company (down 1.66 percent) and Pakistan State Oil (down 2.33 percent) were the biggest drags. All refineries traded down to lower limits after the government shifted higher petrol import costs onto local refineries in the October 31 pricing notification, leaving the ex-depot price unchanged at Rs377.91 a litre.

Why sentiment turned

The positive close came amid a more than 4 percent decline in global oil prices, as Iranian and Qatari officials held a third consecutive day of talks aimed at ending the US-Israeli war on Iran, easing concerns over energy costs and Pakistan's import bill. Trading volume fell to 443.4 million shares from 825.4 million on Friday. October CPI rose 9.6 percent year over year, still above the State Bank's 5-7 percent target range, with resistance at 167,500-168,000 the key level to watch, according to Arif Habib Limited.

articles.title: PSX in October: KSE-100 Fell 3,560 Points as War Fears and a Rate Hike Weighed
articles.description: The KSE-100 closed October at 166,409.25, down 3,560 points or 2.09% for the month, as Middle East tensions, foreign selling and the State Bank's rate rise to 12% outweighed an early-October IMF staff-level deal.
articles.sources: Mettis Global, Shafaqna, Arif Habib Limited, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
The KSE-100 Index closed October 2026 on a weak note, shedding 3,560.08 points, or 2.09 percent, to settle at 166,409.25, as an escalating Middle East conflict kept energy prices elevated and pushed the State Bank of Pakistan into tightening policy in the final week of the month, Mettis Global reported on November 2.

Five weekly losses, then a bounce

The index opened October around 169,969, its September close, and drifted lower for most of four weeks, logging five consecutive weekly losses before a late-month bounce that proved too shallow. October was the market's third losing month out of four in fiscal 2026-27, taking the fiscal-year-to-date loss to 13,892.45 points, or 7.71 percent, from the June close of 180,301.70. Market capitalisation fell to Rs4.66 trillion from Rs4.78 trillion. Foreign investors remained net sellers in October, offloading equities worth $71.26 million.

What drove the fall — and what held up

Even a staff-level agreement with the IMF early in October — paving the way for $1 billion plus $210 million in disbursements, subject to board approval — could not lift the mood for long. The State Bank raised the policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent on October 26, citing higher energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty. Beneath the headline, KSE-100 company earnings rose 26 percent year over year in the first nine months of 2026 to Rs1,638 billion, according to Arif Habib Limited — a reminder, analysts said, that October's fall was driven mostly by worry, not by collapsing profits.

articles.title: Pakistan's Refineries Report 1,860% Profit Jump as War-Driven Margins Surge
articles.description: Pakistan's four listed oil refineries reported a combined net profit above Rs57 billion for the quarter through September, up from Rs2.9 billion a year earlier, as refining margins widened amid global energy disruptions.
articles.sources: Nikkei Asia, PSX disclosures, Sherman Securities, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's major oil refineries reported a nearly twentyfold surge in combined profit for the latest quarter through September, benefiting from increasing refining margins amid global energy disruptions, Nikkei Asia reported on November 1, citing disclosures to the Pakistan Stock Exchange.

The numbers

All four listed refineries reported extraordinary increases in net profit, with their combined net profit exceeding Rs57 billion, compared with Rs2.9 billion in the corresponding quarter last year — a gain of more than 1,860%. The top earner was Attock Refinery, based in Rawalpindi, at Rs18.65 billion after tax, followed by Pakistan Refinery in Karachi at Rs13.97 billion, Cnergyico at Rs12.88 billion and National Refinery at Rs11.57 billion. Pakistan's fifth refinery, Pak-Arab Refinery, is not listed and has not released a financial statement.

A windfall expected to be short-lived

The gains come as fuel prices rise due to the ongoing Middle East conflict between the US and Iran, on top of the Ukraine war, creating a global fuel shortage that has hit Pakistani consumers hard: according to government fuel-price notifications as of October 20, petrol prices had risen 47.6% since the start of the war, while diesel prices had jumped 41.2%. Experts cited in the report said the unusually strong earnings look to be unsustainable, and unlikely to provide the companies sufficient funding for the costly modernisation of the country's ageing refineries, according to a research report by Sherman Securities, a Pakistani brokerage house.

articles.title: PSX Ends Four-Session Rally as Oil Surge Triggers Profit-Taking, Index Closes at 166,409
articles.description: The KSE-100 index fell 784.19 points, or 0.47%, on Friday to close at 166,409, ending a four-session run as Brent crude surged above $116 a barrel on Gulf tensions.
articles.sources: Dawn, Express Tribune, The Nation, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange came under heavy profit-taking on Friday, ending its four-session northward run, Dawn reported on October 31.

A volatile final session

Topline Securities said the market remained largely in negative territory, with the index down 784.19 points, or 0.47%, to close at 166,409 points, against 167,193.44 in the previous session. The index reached an intraday high of 167,339 and a low of 166,535, closing near the day's low after failing to sustain early gains. The top negative contributors — United Bank, Lucky Cement, Habib Bank, Fatima Fertiliser and Attock Refinery — weighed the index down by 359 points, while Engro Fertiliser, Pakistan Oilfield, Meezan Bank, Engro Holdings and OGDC provided support, adding 177 points.

Why sentiment turned

Bearish sentiment was driven mainly by rising crude oil prices, expectations of heightened US-Iran tensions following the US midterm elections, and reported attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude surged above $116 per barrel, and the Finance Division has projected October inflation at 9.5% to 10.5% amid elevated energy prices, with diesel at Rs400.67 and petrol at Rs377.91 per litre. Trading volume edged up 1.05% to 825.46 million shares, though turnover plunged 26.69% to Rs23.12 billion. For the month, the KSE-100 ended October down 2.09%, with brokers citing support near the 160,000 level.

articles.title: Pakistan Cement Makers' Profits Rise 17% to Rs34.2 Billion in First Quarter of FY27
articles.description: Combined profits of PSX-listed cement companies rose 17% year on year to Rs34.2 billion in the first quarter of FY27, as domestic sales grew 10% and gross margins improved to 35.1%.
articles.sources: Profit by Pakistan Today, AKD Research, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
Combined profitability of cement companies listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange increased by 17% year on year to Rs34.2 billion during the first quarter of FY27, compared with Rs29.1 billion in the corresponding period last year, Profit by Pakistan Today reported on October 31, citing AKD Research's sector review.

Domestic demand leads

Total cement dispatches increased by 4% to 8.57 million tonnes from 8.27 million tonnes a year earlier. Domestic dispatches rose 10% to 7.1 million tonnes, increasing their share of total sales to 83% from 78%. Exports, however, declined 20% to 1.5 million tonnes, partly due to the closure of the Afghan border. Combined revenue increased 17% to Rs143.35 billion from Rs122.56 billion, while gross profit grew 25% to Rs50.32 billion, with gross margins improving to 35.1% from 32.9%.

A strong quarter, a weaker export story

Profit before tax increased 17% to Rs49.28 billion, while taxation rose by the same percentage to Rs15.11 billion. On a quarterly basis, revenue rose 15%, gross profit 10% and net profit 18%, while total dispatches rose 12% from 7.68 million tonnes in the preceding quarter. The picture is one of a domestic construction recovery carrying the sector, even as the export channel — hit by the Afghan border closure — continues to drag.

articles.title: Pakistan's Exports Rise 7.7% to $8.5 Billion but Trade Gap Widens in First Quarter
articles.description: Pakistan's exports rose 7.7% to $8.5 billion in the July–September quarter of fiscal 2026-27, but imports grew nearly twice as fast to $17.8 billion, widening the trade deficit to $9.3 billion, official figures show.
articles.sources: Arab News, Finance Division October Economic Update and Outlook, and The Pakistan Daily, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's merchandise exports rose 7.7% to $8.5 billion during July–September, the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27, compared with $7.9 billion in the corresponding period last year, according to figures shared by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and the Finance Division's October Economic Update and Outlook.

Imports grew almost twice as fast

The country's imports of goods rose 14.3% to $17.8 billion in the quarter, while combined imports of goods and services increased 14.6% to $21.3 billion. The result was a quarterly trade deficit of $9.3 billion — larger than the entire quarter's exports. September was stronger on both sides: exports grew 15.5% to $3 billion, while imports grew 22.7% to $6.2 billion. Oil explains much of the import side, with Brent crude averaging $116.8 a barrel in September, up 28.4% from August, and petroleum accounting for about a quarter of total imports in fiscal 2025.

Remittances and reserves cushion the gap

Workers' remittances increased 14% to $10.9 billion in the quarter, compared with $9.5 billion a year earlier, while foreign direct investment rose by nearly 20% to approximately $720 million. By October 16, the State Bank's liquid reserves had reached $21.5 billion, with total liquid foreign reserves at $26.8 billion. The widening trade gap contributed to a current account deficit of $874 million, compared with $755 million in the same period last year.

Inflation and interest rates

Consumer inflation stood at 10.3% in September, down from 11.1% in August but above the 5.8% recorded in September last year. Transport prices increased 27.4% year-on-year, while housing, water, electricity, gas and fuel costs rose 12.4%. The State Bank raised its policy rate by 0.5 percentage points to 12%, effective October 27, 2026, and the Finance Division expects inflation to remain between 9.5% and 10.5% in October.

The government expects around 4% growth this fiscal year, after 3.7% growth in fiscal 2025-26, as it attempts to avoid past cycles in which consumption-driven expansion increased imports and pressured foreign exchange reserves.

articles.title: SIFC Finalises 38 Projects Targeting $40 Billion in Investment, Senate Panel Told
articles.description: The Special Investment Facilitation Council has finalised around 38 projects across major sectors with an estimated investment potential of $40 billion, officials told a Senate committee on October 29, 2026.
articles.sources: Profit by Pakistan Today, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
The Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) has finalised around 38 projects across major sectors of Pakistan's economy, with an estimated investment potential of $40 billion, officials informed the Senate Standing Committee on Cabinet Secretariat on Thursday, according to Profit by Pakistan Today.

Where the projects sit

The projects cover mining, industry, railways, roads, maritime affairs, power, information technology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, tourism and food security, as the government seeks to attract foreign investment and address regulatory obstacles affecting businesses. The committee was also informed that the Brownfield Refinery Policy had been approved, with five refineries signing implementation agreements involving proposed investments of approximately $6 billion.

Who the council is courting

SIFC officials briefed lawmakers on engagement with Chinese companies and prospective investors from Qatar and Kuwait, alongside measures aimed at simplifying regulatory approvals, facilitating visas and introducing single-window services for investors.

The caveats lawmakers raised

The committee, chaired by Senator Rana Mehmoodul Hassan, raised concerns over high business costs, regulatory hurdles and profit repatriation. Senator Abdul Qadir pointed to Pakistan's higher business costs compared with regional economies, particularly electricity prices and financing expenses. Officials also cautioned that disruptions to trade and business arising from the regional situation, including the US-Iran conflict, had made it difficult to provide reliable investment projections and final figures at this stage.

The $40 billion figure is therefore best read as an estimated potential across the project pipeline rather than committed funding, with final outcomes depending on investor decisions and regional stability.

articles.title: PSX Extends Recovery as KSE-100 Closes Above 167,000 on October 29
articles.description: The KSE-100 index closed at 167,193.43 on October 29, 2026, gaining 0.88 percent, as strong quarterly earnings and a steady rupee kept buyers in control at the Pakistan Stock Exchange.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange extended its recovery on Thursday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index reported to close at 167,193.43, up 0.88 percent on the day. The session built on gains from earlier in the week, with buyers active from the opening bell, when the index was reported trading above 166,900 points.

What drove the buying

Market watchers attributed the momentum to robust quarterly earnings announcements and continued stability in the Pakistani rupee. Heavyweight stocks featured prominently, with Pakistan State Oil reported among the strong performers on profit expansion, while Lucky Cement announced significant capacity expansions. Earlier in the week, corporate results from companies including Fauji Fertiliser, National Bank, Hub Power, MCB Bank and Bank Alfalah had already supported the index.

Trading activity and the rupee

Volume on the all-share index rose to 816.83 million shares, with the value of shares traded rising to Rs31.54 billion. Cnergyico PK led the volume chart with 184.01 million shares, followed by Pervez Ahmed Co with 81.15 million shares and K-Electric Ltd with 46.83 million shares. Of 499 companies traded, 232 registered gains, 232 recorded falls and 35 remained unchanged. The Pakistani rupee continued its marginal gain against the US dollar in the inter-bank market, closing at 276.76, a gain of Re0.01 against the greenback.

What to watch next

Analysts quoted in market coverage cautioned that breadth remains mixed even as headline momentum stays positive, with average shares still below their longer-term averages in some readings. For investors, the coming sessions will test whether earnings strength can keep carrying the index higher or whether profit-taking returns at higher levels.

As always, daily index moves reflect a single session's trading and not a forecast for the sessions ahead.

articles.title: Petrol, Diesel Prices Rise From October 29 as Government Revises Fuel Rates
articles.description: Petrol rises by Rs1.85 to Rs377.91 a litre and high-speed diesel by Rs1.75 to Rs399.82 from October 29, 2026, under the government's fortnightly fuel pricing revision.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
The government has increased the price of petrol by Rs1.85 per litre and high-speed diesel by Rs1.75 per litre, with the revised rates effective from October 29, 2026, according to reports from the Petroleum Division. Petrol now costs Rs377.91 per litre, up from Rs376.06, while high-speed diesel costs Rs399.82 per litre, up from Rs398.07.

How the revision was made

According to the Petroleum Division, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) revised the ex-depot prices under the federal government's petroleum pricing mechanism. The division attributed the changes to global developments, including fluctuations in Platts rates, premiums and other incidental charges.

What it means for households and businesses

The increase is expected to raise fuel expenses for households, commuters and businesses already facing high transportation and operating costs. Higher diesel prices may also push up freight and public transport expenses, potentially increasing the cost of goods and services that depend on road transport.

The wider fuel picture

Fuel prices in Pakistan are revised on a fortnightly cycle linked to international market movements and currency trends, so each revision reflects the prevailing global price environment rather than a permanent new level. Consumers and transport operators typically watch the next revision closely, as further movements in global prices or the exchange rate can move pump prices again.

Motorists are advised to check the notified rates at their local fuel stations, as the revised prices apply from October 29.

articles.title: KSE-100 Gains 1,269 Points to Close Above 165,700
articles.description: The benchmark KSE-100 Index gained 1,269.55 points, or 0.77%, to close at 165,736.76 on Wednesday, extending its recovery on broad-based buying.
articles.sources: APP/UrduPoint, ARY News, Business Recorder, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange continued its bullish momentum on Wednesday, gaining 1,269.55 points, a positive change of 0.77 percent, to close at 165,736.76 points against 164,467.20 points in the previous trading session. The index touched an intraday high of 166,100.34 points and a low of 164,355.83 points.

Breadth and volumes

The ready market witnessed trading volume of 578.124 million shares, up from 401.969 million in the previous session, while traded value increased to Rs26.203 billion from Rs18.069 billion. Market capitalisation rose to Rs18.329 trillion from Rs18.214 trillion. Of 496 companies traded, 269 posted gains, 180 suffered losses and 47 remained unchanged. Pervez Ahmed Co led the volume chart with 58.321 million shares, followed by TPL Properties with 38.349 million and Cnergyico PK with 34.763 million shares.

Among the top gainers, Ghandhara Industries surged Rs106.12 to close at Rs1,167.28, while Rafhan Maize advanced Rs70.86 to Rs8,408.05. On the losing side, PIA Holding Company LimitedB fell Rs448.49 to Rs13,551.50. The rupee also edged up, closing at 276.77 against the US dollar, a gain of Re0.03. The rally extended Tuesday's recovery, which Business Recorder attributed to easing international crude prices and broad-based buying despite the State Bank's recent 50-basis-point rate hike.

articles.title: Fauji Fertilizer's Nine-Month Profit Hits Rs71 Billion on Strong Urea Demand
articles.description: Fauji Fertilizer Company reported consolidated nine-month profit of Rs71.02 billion as revenue climbed nearly 15.7% to Rs373.24 billion.
articles.sources: Daily Pakistan, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
Fauji Fertilizer Company (FFC) has reported a strong nine-month performance, with consolidated profit climbing to Rs71.02 billion, nearly Rs8 billion higher than a year earlier, on the back of stronger fertilizer demand and investment income. Standalone nine-month profit reached approximately Rs64.16 billion.

The numbers

Consolidated revenue climbed to approximately Rs373.24 billion during the nine-month period, growth of nearly 15.7%. Gross profit increased around 14.9% to Rs124.64 billion, while operating profit advanced 13.9% to approximately Rs92.08 billion. Profit before taxation stood at Rs108.62 billion, with a tax expense of nearly Rs37.60 billion. Rising borrowing costs remained a concern, with finance expenses increasing about 37.1% to Rs7.60 billion.

Operational figures showed stronger demand for key products: urea offtake increased to approximately 2.16 million tonnes from 1.96 million tonnes a year earlier, and prilled urea production at Goth Machhi and Mirpur Mathelo rose around 2% to 1.91 million tonnes. Gas supply constraints, however, cut granular urea production by about 15% to 281,000 tonnes, and Sona DAP production fell to 586,000 tonnes from 622,000 amid raw material availability challenges and elevated phosphoric acid prices. On the stock exchange, FFC shares were trading near Rs549-550 on October 28, compared with about Rs537 in the previous session. The growth comes as the company continues to benefit from its expanded operations following the merger with Fauji Fertilizer Bin Qasim Limited.

articles.title: KSE-100 Climbs 1,428 Points to Close at 164,467 in Bullish Session
articles.description: The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange gained 1,428.73 points on Tuesday to close at 164,467.20, with 282 companies advancing and traded value rising to Rs18.069 billion.
articles.sources: UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News (APP), October 27, 2026.
articles.body:
The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange continued its bullish momentum on Tuesday, gaining 1,428.73 points, a positive change of 0.88 percent, to close at 164,467.20 points against 163,038.47 points recorded in the previous trading session, Associated Press of Pakistan reported.

The ready market witnessed a trading volume of 401.969 million shares, compared with 376.019 million shares traded in the previous session, while the traded value increased to Rs18.069 billion from Rs16.192 billion. Market capitalisation increased to Rs18.214 trillion from Rs18.061 trillion recorded a day earlier.

Breadth and leading stocks

Out of 497 companies that traded in the ready market, 282 posted gains, 170 suffered losses, while 45 remained unchanged. K-Electric Ltd led the volume chart with 54.027 million shares, followed by Cnergyico PK with 30.699 million shares and WorldCall Telecom with 24.034 million shares.

Among the top gainers, Ghandhara Industries Limited surged by Rs96.47 to close at Rs1,061.16, while Pakistan Tobacco Company Limited advanced by Rs73.63 to settle at Rs1,473.58. On the losing side, Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited declined by Rs162.81 to close at Rs8,337.19, while Khairpur Sugar Mills Limited fell by Rs139.98 to Rs1,259.84.

Futures market also active

In the futures market, turnover stood at 455.777 million shares with a traded value of Rs14.653 billion, compared with 339.047 million shares worth Rs9.357 billion in the previous session. Of 313 companies traded in the futures market, 247 advanced, 63 declined and 3 remained unchanged.

The strong session came on a day of major economic news, with the State Bank of Pakistan's policy rate decision taking effect and investors tracking corporate results and macroeconomic signals. Market watchers will look to coming sessions to see whether the bullish momentum holds.

Market breadth was clearly positive, with advancers comfortably outnumbering decliners in both the ready and futures segments. The rise in traded value alongside the index gain suggests participation broadened rather than resting on a handful of stocks, a pattern traders often read as a healthier session than a narrow, low-volume advance.

articles.title: Pakistan Signs $2.25 Billion Deal for Lithium Battery Gigafactory in Rawalpindi
articles.description: A $2.25 billion agreement has been signed for a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Rawalpindi, a project backers say could cut import costs, support electric mobility and open export opportunities.
articles.sources: Profit by Pakistan Today, October 27, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan has signed a $2.25 billion agreement for a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Rawalpindi, Profit by Pakistan Today reported on October 27. The agreement was signed by MHIL with Chinese and local investors, and the project remains pending policy approval, according to the report.

The development comes as the government moves towards implementing the Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-2031, recently approved by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif but awaiting clearance from the International Monetary Fund over proposed tax incentives for electric vehicle manufacturing.

Demand outlook to 2030

Engineering Development Board chief Mansoor said Pakistan's demand for battery energy storage systems could reach 100,000 MW by June 2030 if economic growth reaches 5 percent or higher, compared with an estimated 80,000 MW under a growth scenario below 3 percent. He said grid stabilisation alone could require 3,000 to 5,000 MW of battery storage, while meeting overall demand would require four to five gigafactories costing approximately $1 billion to $1.25 billion each.

Pakistan currently assembles around 3,000 to 4,000 MW of batteries, along with components such as motors, controllers and chargers, according to the EDB chief. The agreement would also require manufacturers to export a specified share of their production and comply with international safety and performance standards.

Why local production matters

Mansoor said local battery production would help reduce import costs, support the country's transition towards electric mobility and create opportunities for exports. Battery storage is increasingly central to managing variable renewable energy and stabilising grids, and local manufacturing would reduce dependence on imported cells and packs.

For the project to move from agreement to construction, the pending policy approvals, including the IMF clearance on tax incentives, will be closely watched by investors and the auto industry alike.

The project also fits a broader regional pattern, with countries across Asia investing in battery manufacturing to secure supply chains for electric vehicles and grid storage. For Pakistan, success would mean not only import substitution but a new industrial export line, provided the policy framework, including the pending tax-incentive clearances, is settled in a way investors can rely on.

articles.title: Gold Prices Rise by Rs1,400 per Tola in Pakistan on Monday
articles.description: Gold prices edged higher in Pakistan on October 26, with 24-karat gold rising by Rs1,400 per tola to Rs423,436, according to market reports from Karachi.
articles.sources: Abb Takk News, October 26, 2026.
articles.body:
Gold prices edged higher in Pakistan on Monday, October 26, with the price of 24-karat gold increasing by Rs1,400 per tola to Rs423,436, according to market reports from Karachi. The rise continues a pattern in which local gold prices closely track international bullion movements and shifts in the rupee, making the yellow metal one of the most closely watched prices in Pakistani households and bazaars.

Why gold matters in Pakistan

Gold holds a special place in Pakistan's economy and culture. It is bought for weddings, gifted at family occasions and held by many households as a store of value that can be sold quickly in an emergency. Jewellers in Karachi, Lahore and other trading centres adjust their rates daily, and even a modest move of Rs1,400 per tola is noticed immediately by buyers and sellers. For families planning weddings, the timing of a purchase can change the final bill by thousands of rupees, which is why daily price updates draw such a wide audience.

What drives the local price

Local gold prices are shaped mainly by two forces: the international price of gold in dollars and the value of the rupee against the dollar. When global prices rise, or the rupee weakens, the rupee price of gold in Pakistan tends to climb even if nothing has changed in local demand. Regional tensions and uncertainty can also push investors towards gold as a safe haven, adding further upward pressure. Monday's increase should therefore be read as part of that wider picture rather than as a purely local event, although local demand ahead of the wedding season can amplify moves in either direction.

What buyers should keep in mind

For buyers, the practical lesson is familiar: prices move daily, and small daily changes add up over weeks. Jewellers advise checking the day's official rate before buying and confirming the purity and making charges separately, since the headline per-tola rate is only part of the final price. For investors, gold's appeal lies in its long record as a hedge, but it pays no interest or dividend, and its price can fall as well as rise. Monday's rise is a single day's move, not a forecast, and anyone buying gold as an investment should weigh it against other options rather than chasing one day's headline.

The wider market picture

The gold rise comes on a day when other economic signals were mixed, with business confidence reported to have softened in October even as manufacturing capacity use improved. Taken together, the picture is of an economy still finding its footing: households and firms hedging with gold while waiting for clearer signals on growth, inflation and interest rates. Gold's next move will likely follow global prices and the rupee, and traders will be watching both closely through the week.

articles.title: Business Confidence Falls to 48 in October, State Bank Survey Shows
articles.description: Overall business confidence weakened further in October 2026, with the Business Confidence Index falling 1.1 points to 48, led by a decline in services sector sentiment, the State Bank's latest survey showed.
articles.sources: Mettis Global News, October 26, 2026; State Bank of Pakistan Business Confidence Survey.
articles.body:
Overall business confidence weakened further in October 2026, with the Business Confidence Index falling 1.1 points to 48, led by a decline in services sector sentiment, the State Bank of Pakistan's latest survey showed. The survey, conducted by the State Bank in collaboration with the Institute of Business Administration, ran from October 1 to 14, 2026, and covered 491 respondents.

Services drag, industry steadies

The Services sector index slipped 1.6 points to 47.7, while the Industry sector index edged up 0.2 points to 48.7. The Current Business Confidence Index, which reflects views on general economic conditions over the past six months, eased 1.1 points to 45.4. The Expected Business Confidence Index, which captures the outlook for the next six months, fell 1.2 points to 50.5, sitting just above the neutral threshold. A reading below 50 generally signals that more businesses are pessimistic than optimistic, so the overall figure of 48 points to a cautiously negative mood, even though expectations for the future remain marginally positive.

Purchasing managers and inflation

The Purchasing Managers Index also eased 1.4 points to 51.8, though it stayed above the neutral threshold, suggesting that overall business activity was still expanding, if more slowly. Order books rose to 51.9, the one component to improve, while business activity fell to 50.3, total employees to 48.7, raw material purchases to 55 and speed of suppliers' delivery to 53.2. Aggregate inflation expectations eased to 7.1 percent from 7.7 percent in the previous wave, even though the share of businesses expecting higher prices edged up to 70 percent from 69.8 percent. In industry, that share rose to 71.4 percent from 69.5 percent, while in services it fell to 68.9 percent from 70.1 percent.

Jobs and capacity

Employment sentiment weakened. The Current Employment Index fell to 45.4 from 48.9 in September, while the Expected Employment Index eased to 50.4 from 53.1. There was one brighter spot: in manufacturing, average current capacity utilisation rose to 67.9 percent from 64.8 percent in the previous wave, suggesting factories are using more of their installed capacity even as hiring sentiment cools. That combination, busier plants but weaker hiring, is consistent with firms meeting existing orders cautiously while holding back on new recruitment until demand looks more secure.

What it means

For policymakers, the survey paints a mixed picture rather than a collapse. Activity is still expanding according to the purchasing managers' measure, inflation expectations are moderating, and factories are busier. But confidence, especially in services, is slipping, and employment sentiment is softening. The next survey round will show whether October's dip was a pause or the start of a longer slide, and businesses will be watching interest rates, energy costs and demand conditions for the signal that tips sentiment back above 50.

articles.title: Diesel Raised to Rs393.66 a Litre, Petrol Unchanged at Rs377.71
articles.description: High-speed diesel rose Rs1.91 for October 24-26 while petrol held steady, as Brent crude climbed to $114.57 a barrel on Middle East supply concerns.
articles.sources: TradersUnion; Business Recorder; The Express Tribune, October 23, 2026.
articles.body:
The federal government has increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre while keeping the price of petrol unchanged, under the latest petroleum pricing review. According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol would continue to be sold at Rs377.71 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs393.66 per litre from October 24 to October 26.

The numbers in detail

Following the revision, HSD rises to Rs393.66 per litre from Rs391.75, while the price of motor spirit (petrol) remains unchanged at Rs377.71 per litre. The revised prices remain effective from October 24 to October 26, 2026. The Petroleum Division said the change was necessitated by global developments, including movements in Platts rates, premiums and incidentals. The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs1.60 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel by Rs1.64 per litre for October 23 — making this the second consecutive diesel increase in two days.

Why prices are moving daily now

On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies. The global backdrop to this revision was stark: Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2%, to reach $114.57 a barrel on Friday, touching $115 earlier in the session, its highest level since May 4 and a peak of more than five months, amid concerns about further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East following Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel, according to published breakdowns of the price.

Who feels a diesel rise most

The increase in diesel prices will raise fuel costs for transporters, farmers and other consumers dependent on diesel-powered vehicles and machinery, while petrol consumers will see no change in prices during the three-day period. Diesel matters especially for freight, agriculture and public transport, so even small increases can pass through to food and goods prices. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices, covering an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries. For now, though, the diesel-dependent parts of the economy — the trucks, tractors and buses — face another, if modest, cost increase.

articles.title: FBR Activates Faceless Tax Audit System From October 15
articles.description: Designated income tax and sales tax cases now move through the National Faceless Centre, with audit, assessment and quality control handled by separate officers and all filings electronic via IRIS.
articles.sources: TradersUnion; Business Recorder; Profit by Pakistan Today, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan's Federal Board of Revenue has put into effect a new procedural framework for designated tax cases through the National Faceless Centre, effective October 15, 2026. The move extends across both income tax and sales tax procedures and adds electronic documentation and quality-control checks to the process, in what officials present as a bid to make tax proceedings faster, fairer and more transparent.

What the new framework covers

According to SRO 1828(I)/2026, the FBR has enforced Chapter XX of the Income Tax Rules, 2002, while SRO 1825(I)/2026 brings Chapter VIAC of the Sales Tax Rules, 2006, into effect from the same date. Under the income tax rules, the faceless mechanism applies to cases designated under Section 122E of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, rather than automatically covering every taxpayer. The covered proceedings include audits under Sections 177 and 214C, proceedings under Section 111 and assessments under Chapter X of the Ordinance. The sales tax chapter covers audit under sections 25 and 72B of the Sales Tax Act and proceedings under section 11E. The rules also cover proceedings relating to penalties under Section 182 and default surcharge under Section 205 of the Income Tax Ordinance.

Separation of duties, and everything electronic

The rules require that audit, assessment and quality-control responsibilities for the same case and tax year be handled by separate officers or units. FBR says this functional segregation is designed to strengthen transparency and procedural oversight within the faceless system, so that no single officer controls a case from audit to final order. Notices, orders and other official communications must be generated through the FBR's computerised system and carry a Digital Identification Number (DIN). Taxpayers and their authorised representatives will be required to submit replies, supporting documents and evidence electronically through their designated IRIS accounts. Audit reports, adjudication notices and assessment orders will undergo quality-control reviews under the prescribed procedures.

What has not changed — and what to watch

The framework also allows physical verification through the Field Operations Wing where necessary, subject to authorisation, and cases may be transferred to another tax authority in specified circumstances requiring physical records, repeated verification or special handling. One caution is worth stating plainly: the notifications bring the chapters into force, but as of mid-October reporting, no published order had yet listed which specific cases are assigned to the centre, and no transition rule for audits already open had been found. For taxpayers, the practical step is unchanged in spirit but new in form: keep returns and wealth statements reconciled with FBR's own data, and be ready to respond through IRIS rather than in person. Whether faceless audits deliver on the promise of fairness will be judged by the first cases that go through them.

articles.title: Pakistan-Iran Trade Disruption Puts $2.8 Billion Annual Trade at Stake
articles.description: With border crossings closed since October 17, the LPG halt is only the most visible part of a much larger trade relationship — including about $684 million of Pakistani exports.
articles.sources: Reuters, October 23, 2026; Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
articles.body:
The closure of the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings between Pakistan and Iran, in place since October 17, is about much more than gas cylinders. Pakistan-Iran trade totalled about $2.8 billion in the 2023-24 fiscal year, including roughly $684 million of Pakistani exports, according to the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Every day the crossings stay shut, that trade — and the livelihoods behind it — is at risk.

What crosses the border

The most urgent flow is energy: Pakistan imports about 7,000 metric tons of LPG a day from Iran, according to the Pakistan LPG Association, with more than 4,000 tons a day entering through Gabd-Rimdan alone. But the crossings also carry food and farm produce in both directions. More than 1,000 Pakistani containers carrying potatoes, bananas and rice for Iran were reported stranded when the crossings closed, and hundreds of trucks, including LPG tankers, are stranded on both sides of the border. The Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry has advised members to stop placing new orders with Iran until further notice — a signal of how uncertain traders consider the outlook.

Why the crossings closed

The Balochistan government, in the province where the crossings are located, said the temporary closure was intended to address security concerns and curb smuggling, while Iran's foreign ministry cited technical issues. The differing explanations matter because they point to different paths back to normal: a security-driven closure may reopen once authorities are satisfied, while a technical dispute may need a different kind of fix. There was partial movement during the week, with Gabd-Rimdan reopening for Pakistani exports of perishable goods — a lifeline for exporters of fresh produce, but not yet a full restoration of two-way trade.

What a prolonged closure would cost

For households, the visible cost is already clear: traders said the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder had risen to 7,000 rupees from 4,500 rupees within days. For exporters, the cost is spoiled produce and broken delivery commitments; for transporters, days of waiting with limited access to basic amenities. Pakistan LPG Association chairman Irfan Khokhar warned shortages and price increases could worsen if the disruptions persist. The $2.8 billion headline figure is an annual total, not a daily loss — but it frames the stakes: these are not marginal crossings. They are a working trade artery for Balochistan and beyond, and both countries have an economic interest in getting it flowing again.
